<main class="site-main project-detail" id="content"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Project · R package</p><h1>OrdinalRegressionViz</h1><p class="project-lede">Visual tools that connect model parameters to latent evidence, response thresholds, and uncertainty.</p><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">Published</span><span>Updated 16 Jun 2026</span></div></section><figure class="project-figure"><img src="/assets/sdt-distributions-example.png" alt="Latent signal and noise distributions with ordered response thresholds"><figcaption>Latent distributions and the thresholds that convert evidence into response categories.</figcaption></figure><article class="project-case-study"><section><p class="section-number">Question</p><h2>How can an ordinal model become inspectable?</h2><p>Ordinal regression parameters are easier to discuss when the latent evidence, response criteria, and resulting categories can be seen together.</p></section><section><p class="section-number">What I built</p><h2>Plots and measures.</h2><p>The package draws latent distributions, ROC curves, posterior predictive checks, and Bayesian forest plots. It also computes d′, criteria, scale ratios, and AUC.</p></section><section><p class="section-number">Key design decision</p><h2>Keep the thresholds visible.</h2><p>The visual language connects the coefficients to the response rule instead of treating the fitted model as a black box.</p></section><section><p class="section-number">Artifact</p><p><a class="button-link" href="https://github.com/tomerzipori/OrdinalRegressionViz#readme">Open the package README</a></p></section><section><p class="section-number">Limitations</p><h2>A plot is not a design.</h2><p>A clear figure cannot repair weak data, an unexamined coding choice, or an unsupported causal claim.</p></section></article>
